s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like facial pain with trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by specific movements
salient_findings: Severe pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Attacks triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Received third dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Pain started the day after vaccination
Pain initially affected the entire left hemiface
Pain localized to V2 and V3 distributions within days
Attacks last 4-5 seconds
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Normal sensory testing
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Normal routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections was negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by jaw movement

shortlist.label: Classical trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, sharp pain with normal sensory testing and no other neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, episodic pain with trigeminal nerve distribution, although less likely due to specific V2 and V3 involvement

shortlist.label: Secondary trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Pain started after vaccination, potentially indicating a secondary cause, but normal MRI reduces likelihood

shortlist.label: Painful trigeminal neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe pain and allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch, consistent with neuropathic pain

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, and reaching 10/10 on a numeric pain scale, are characteristic of classical trigeminal neuralgia. The absence of other neurological deficits and normal sensory testing also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Trigeminal neuralgia
rejected.why: Too broad, as classical trigeminal neuralgia is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
rejected.why: The pain is localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the trigeminal nerve, not the glossopharyngeal nerve

rejected.label: Secondary trigeminal neuralgia
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a underlying cause, such as a tumor or multiple sclerosis, and the contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities

rejected.label: Painful trigeminal neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not suggest a neuropathy, as sensory testing was normal and the pain is episodic and triggered by specific actions
